la:verb:surgo.html:
surgo and surrĭgo (subr-): surrexi and subrexi, surrectum and subrectum, 3 (
perf. surregit, Paul. ex Müll.; orig. forms: surrigit,; : surriguntur, id. Ira, 1, 1 med.: surrigebant, Hier. Vit. Hil. fin.: subrigens,; : subrigere, . — Sync. forms: surrexti,: surrexe,), v. a. and n.
contr. from surrigo, from sub-rego
.
Act., to lift or raise up, to raise, erect, elevate (very rare; after the Aug. per., the original uncontracted forms were chiefly used in this sense, to distinguish it from the class. signif., II.): plaudite, valete: lumbos surgite atque extollite,: caput,: omnes capitum hiatus ( = capita hiantia),: surgit caput Apenninus,: tot surrigit aures,: terrae motus defert montes, surrigit plana, valles extuberat,: paulatim subrigens se,: cristam,: cornua,; cf. mid.: horrent et surriguntur capilli,rise, stand erect,: hastae surrectā cuspide in terrā fixae,: mucrone surrecto,: calcar equo,: aures subrectae furentibus,: turres subrectae,: surrecta moles,.—
Neutr., to rise, arise, to get up, stand up (the predominant and class. signif. of the word; syn.: exsurgo, exorior).
Lit.
In gen.: a mensā surgunt saturi, poti,: a cenā,: e lecto,: e lectulo,: de sellā,: ex subselliis,: solio,: humo,; : toro,: toris,: ab umbris ad lumina vitae,.— Esp., of an orator: cur, cum tot summi oratores sedeant, ego potissimum surrexerim,: ad dicendum,; : ad respondendum,: surgit ad hos Ajax,.—Absol.: nolo eum, qui dicturus est, sollicitum surgere,: secundā vigiliā surgit,breaks up the camp, marches,.—
Of things, to rise, mount up, ascend (mostly poet.; syn. ascendo): surgat pius ignis ab arā,: jussit subsidere valles ... lapidosos surgere montes,: mons Rhipaeus,: Atlas,. — Of the sea: fretum,: mare,: aequora,: undae,: amoeni fontes,: cacumina oleae in altum,: fistula disparibus avenis,; cf. poet.: surgens in cornua cervus ( = ferens cornua ardua),i. e. towering,: umeri surgunt,: lux Praecipitatur aquis et aquis nox surgit ab isdem,; : sol,: dies,: luna,: tenebrae,: austri,: ventus,: quae (aedes) proxima surgit ovili,stands,.—
In partic.
To rise, arise, get up from bed, from sleep: ille multo ante lucem surrexit,: ante lucem,, a: cum die,: mane ad invisas rotas,: ad lites novas,: ad praescripta munia,.—
To rise in growth, to spring up, grow up; to rise in building, be built, etc. (poet. and in post - Aug. prose): venerata Ceres culmo surgeret alto,: nec potuere surgere messes,: harundo,: sementis,: surgens arx,; cf.: nunc aggere multo Surgit opus,: area cinere mixtisque pumicibus oppleta surrexerat,: Ascanius surgens,growing,.—
To ascend, go up: ad auras Aetherias,i. e. into life,.—
Trop., to rise, arise, occur, etc. (poet. and in post-Aug. prose): multum supra prosam orationem surgit,: quae nunc animo sententia surgit?: pugna aspera surgit,: discordia,: rumor,: honor,: ingenium suis velocius annis,: non ulla laborum nova mi facies surgit,.—Of the swell of a verse: sex mihi surgat opus numeris; in quinque residat (cf.: "in the hexameter rises the fountain's silvery column," Coleridge),. —
With in or ad and acc., to rise to or against, to attempt, assume, attack, etc. (poet. and late Lat.): in Teucros Aetolis surgit ab Arpis Tydides,: surrecturus in vires, si ipse quoque lacesseretur, Amm. 31, 3, 4: Procopius in res surrexerat novas,: ad motum certaminum civilium avide surrecturus,: ad insontium pericula surrexerunt,; .

la:adv:sursum.html:
sursum (collat. form sursus, : susum, ; Aug. Tract. 8, Ep. 1, Joan. 2; Tract. 10, 5; :
SVRVORSVM,), adv.
contr. from sub-vorsum
, from below, i. e. up, upwards, on high (opp. deorsum; class. and very freq.).
Denoting motion: cum ex alto puteo sursum ad summum escenderis,: ascendere in tectum,: illuc,: quid nunc supina sursum in caelum conspicis?: subducere susum animam,; cf. infra, II.: flammae expressae sursum (opp. deorsum ferri),: adspicit nil sursum,: sursum ac deorsum diducere, Tubero ap. ; .—
Pleon. joined with versus (versum, vorsum), : vineam sursum vorsum semper ducito,; : sursus enim vorsus gignuntur et augmina sumunt: Et sursum nitidae fruges arbustaque crescunt,: cum gradatim sursum versus reditur,; so, sursum versus,; ; ; —
Sursum deorsum, up and down, to and fro: sursum deorsum ultro citroque commeantibus,: ne sursum deorsum cursites,.—Prov.: omnia ista sursum deorsum fortuna versavit,topsy-turvy,; cf.: quod sursum est, deorsum faciunt,i. e. they turn every thing upside down,—
Denoting situation or locality, high up, above (very rare): qui colunt deorsum, magis aestate laborant; qui sursum, magis hieme ... nec non sursum quam deorsum tardius seruntur ac metuntur,: praeterito hac rectā plateā sursum,: nares, quod omnis odor ad supera fertur, recte sursum sunt,.

la:adj:surdus.html:
surdus, a, um, adj.
Sanscr. svar, heavy; svaras, weight; cf. O. H. Germ. swārida, weight
,
deaf.
Lit.: ne mi ut surdo verbera auris,; : si surdus sit, varietates vocum noscere possit?: utinam aut hic surdus aut haec muta facta sit,.—Sup., stone-deaf, ; .—Prov.: surdo narrare, canere, etc., preach to deaf ears, talk to the wind: nae ille haud scit, quam mihi nunc surdo narret fabulam,: cantabant surdo, cf.: non canimus surdis,; and: quae (praecepta) vereor, ne vana surdis auribus cecinerim,; ; : narrare asello Fabellam surdo,; cf.: suadere surdis, quid sit opus facto,.—
Transf.
Deaf to any thing, i. e. not listening, unwilling to hear, inattentive, regardless, insensible, inexorable; also, not understanding, not apprehending: orando surdas jam aures reddideras mihi,; so, aures,; cf. (3, 8), 48; (3, 13), 13: non surdus judex, (7, 15): ad mea munera surdus,: per numquam surdos in tua vota deos,: surdae ad omnia solacia aures,: surdae ad fortia consilia Vitellio aures,: surdus adversus aliquid,: surdus sum,I will not hear,: surdas clamare ad undas,: litora,—Hence, poet. transf.: vota,i. e. to which the gods are deaf, to which they will not hearken,: surdaeque adhibent solatia menti,: tuas lacrimas litora surda bibent,leges rem surdam, inexorabilem esse,: surda tellus,not susceptible of cultivation,: surdus timori,not capable of fear,: tuis lacrimis,: in alicujus sermone,.—Comp.: scopulis surdior Icari Voces audit adhuc integer (i. e. castus),: surdior illa freto surgente,: surdior aequoribus,: non saxa surdiora navitis,.—
With gen.: Mars genitor, votorum haud surde meorum,: pactorum,: veritatis,.—
Of things that give out a dull, indistinct sound, dull-sounding (very rare): theatrum, Müll.: locus,: loca,: vox,: surdum quiddam et barbarum,.—
Pass., that is not heard, noiseless, silent, still, mute, dumb (poet. and in post-Aug. prose): lyra,buccina,: plectra,: non erit officii gratia surda tui,unsung,; cf. fama,: surdum et ignobile opus,: nomen parentum,: herbae,: quos diri conscia facti mens surdo verbere caedit,secret,: ictus,.—
Of odor, appearance, meaning, etc., faint, dim, dull, indistinct, stupid: spirant cinnama surdum,: colos,: hebes unitate surdā color,: discrimen figurarum,: materia,: res surdae ac sensu carentes,; so ; .—Hence, * adv.: surdē, faintly, imperfectly, indistinctly: surde audire, Afran. ap. P. (Com. Fragm. v. 348 Rib.).

la:verb:surripio.gloss: to snatch away; to steal, pilfer, purloin, filch
senses: to snatch away; to steal, pilfer, purloin, filch
la:verb:surripio.html:
sur-rĭpĭo (subr-), rĭpŭi (rŭpŭi, ; ;
v. Ritschl, Proleg. p. xcv.), reptum, 3 (sync. forms: surpite,: surpere,: surpuit,; ; 5, 4, 14: surpuerit,: surpuerat,; perf. subj. surrepsit for surripuerit, ), v. a. and n.
rapio
, to snatch or take away secretly, to withdraw privily, to steal, pilfer, purloin (class.).
Lit.: qui vasa ex privato sacro surripuerit,: ex ejus custodiā filium,: libros servus. : puerum (servos),; cf. surreptus (puer),; : filius ex patriā,: sacram coronam Jovis,: de mille fabae modiis unum,: mappam praetori surpuit,.—Of literary theft: qui a Naevio vel sumpsisti multa, si fateris, vel, si negas, surripuisti,: Ennium hoc ait Homero surripuisse, Ennio Vergilium,: non surripiendi causā, sed palam imitandi,: surrupuisti te mihi dudum de foro,i. e. you have stolen away from me,; cf. : quae (puella) se surpuerat mihi,: unum me surpite morti,.—Absol.: quare, Si quidvis satis est, perjuras, surripis, aufers Undique?. —
Trop.: virtus, quae nec eripi nec surripi potest,: aut occulte surripi aut impune eripi,: surripiendum aliquid putavi spatii,: motus quoque surpere debent,: crimina oculis patris,: diem,: tempus quod adhuc subripiebatur, collige et serva,.

In partic., a scion, graft, a sucker, slip, set of a plant for growth: da mihi ex istā arbore quos seram surculos,; ; ; ; .—
A small tree, ; ; ; 9, 4, 2; : fructus surculorum,.
